{
  "claim": "recover_json_object does not apply last-wins duplicate-key parsing to fenced candidates, so a later fenced object with repeated keys is skipped and an earlier strict fenced object is returned, contrary to the rule that any candidate parsing as strict JSON or last-wins is scoreable and the last fenced scoreable object is chosen.",
  "expected": "For content with two ```json fences, first {\"b\": 3} and second {\"a\": 1, \"a\": 2}, recover_json_object returns ({\"a\": 2}, (\"a\",)) because the second fenced object is scoreable via last-wins and is the last fenced scoreable object.",
  "observed": "The code sets parsed = None for fenced candidates when strict parsing fails, so the second fenced object is skipped; the first fenced object {\"b\": 3} is returned as ({\"b\": 3}, ()).",
  "reproducer": "```json\n{\"b\": 3}\n```\n```json\n{\"a\": 1, \"a\": 2}\n```",
  "source_basis": "A candidate that parses as strict JSON, or as JSON with repeated keys resolved last-wins, is scoreable; The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one.",
  "execution_evidence": "none: no executable oracle",
  "scope": "Replies with multiple fenced JSON objects where the last fenced object contains duplicate keys and an earlier fenced object is strict JSON.",
  "uncertainty": "None; the documented rule does not exclude fenced candidates from last-wins resolution."
}
